title: Google Is Testing Paying Sites for AI Answers: The AI Contribution Pilot Explained

blocks.text: Google Is Testing Paying Sites for AI Answers: The AI Contribution Pilot Explained

Google is testing payments to websites whose content significantly shapes answers in Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode, with earnings shown in Search Console. Here is what the pilot is, what is confirmed, and what our own Generative AI report shows.

Google is running a test where it pays some websites when their content shapes an AI answer. It is called the AI contribution pilot. It lives inside Search Console, it covers Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode, and only a limited group of publishers can see it so far.

The change matters because of what it says about the deal. Until now the arrangement has been that you write, Google might index you, and maybe you get a click. In this pilot, you write, the AI answers get better, and you get paid for your part.
The old deal and the new one
Our summary of the pilot as reported by Search Engine Land and Search Engine Journal.
What the AI contribution pilot is

Google's own help page describes it in one sentence: the pilot lets you earn money when your content contributes significantly to the creation of AI-generated responses shown to users in participating products.
Google Search Console help page titled About AI contribution pilot, with the earn money sentence highlighted Google's help page for the pilot, screenshot captured September 19, 2026.
Three details on that page do most of the work:
Where you can earn. The Gemini app, AI Overviews and AI Mode.

What counts. Google says AI contribution is about the phase where web content can significantly influence what response gets generated. A page that only confirms a fact, or gets linked after the response exists, does not qualify.
How you track it. A pilot report in Search Console shows your earnings and last payment, and you can join or leave at any time from Search Console settings.

What is confirmed and what is not

Reporting from Search Engine Journal and Search Engine Land says Google confirmed this is an early-stage pilot. At least dozens of publishers have been approached, though the total was not confirmed. It shows up as an opt-in panel in Search Console for a limited number of sites, and it was first spotted in April 2026.

Publishers in it see a monthly earnings figure in Search Console. They get little detail on how Google reached that number, and Playwire describes the payouts as real money and a black box. Some coverage describes early amounts as small next to ad revenue.

Google has reportedly run similar programs with some news publishers around the world, as negotiated deals. This pilot looks like an attempt to go beyond news and reach other kinds of sites with a standard program, closer to a creator rewards scheme than a licensing contract.

Why we care, and what we can show
We are not in the pilot as far as we can tell, and we have no payout to show you. Nothing in this post claims earnings.

What we can show is how much AI surfaces already draw on our content. Search Console's Generative AI features report (still labelled beta) counts impressions in AI features. Here is our main site and our SEO product site over the last three months.
Impressions in the Generative AI report, Search Console, last 3 months (June 17 to September 15, 2026)
Source: our own Search Console Generative AI features report (beta), screenshots captured September 19, 2026. Impressions, not earnings.

Search Console Generative AI features report for ManasFlow.com showing 1M total impressions over 3 months ManasFlow.com, Generative AI features report, June 17 to September 15, 2026. Daily impressions start around 4K and peak near 23K in mid August.

Search Console Generative AI features report for manasrank.com showing 15.3K total impressions over 3 months manasrank.com, same report and period. Near zero until late July, then up to about 900 impressions a day in late August.

Two things stand out. The main site's daily figure climbed from about 4K to a peak near 23K. And manasrank.com went from near zero to about 900 daily AI impressions in roughly a month. Impressions are not contribution, and contribution is not earnings. The report tells you where AI features already show your pages. It does not tell you whether you would qualify.

What to do this week
Check Search Console for an AI contribution panel. If it is there, you were invited. If not, you are like most sites right now.
Open the Generative AI features report. Look at which pages get AI impressions. Those are the pages that already show up in AI features, which is a useful starting list.

Write for the generation step, not the click. The pilot pays for content that shapes an answer as it is written. That favors original data, current facts and clear definitions over recycled summaries.
Keep pages fresh and factual. Freshness is a reasonable bet, since the pilot is about content that shapes the answer while it is written. A stale page is a weak candidate.
Do not restructure your whole site for a pilot. It is a test with unclear payouts. The work above also helps normal search and AI citations, so it pays off either way.
Our read
If Google scales this, sites would get paid for being useful inside an answer, and not only when someone clicks through. That is a real change in incentives for anyone who publishes.
It is also still a test. The payout method is opaque, the group is small and the amounts are reportedly modest. Treat it as a signal about direction, not a revenue line to plan around.
